I don't think it's helpful to have the entry with a hexadecimal base number with a negative sign. That's rarely done, and the value shown in most specifications (whether https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#encodings or https://www.iana.org/assignments/rfb/rfb.xhtml#rfb-4) is 0xC0A1E5CE

It's a lot easier to read and remember 0xC0A1E5CE anyway, because it's clearly leetspeak for the word "coalesce".

value_strings are natively 32 bit unsigned integers anyway (cf. #20305 - luckily VNC uses 32 bit). That matters if the value string is eventually turned into a value_string_ext, because putting it in the proper order means that binary search could be used.

Isn't it simply the general custom of the VNC specification that actual encodings are positive, whereas psuedo-encodings/extensions are negative? (edit. - Well, I suppose extensions are anything greater than 0x40000000, perhaps?)

If you want to comment that to document it, that seems reasonable but it applies in general to all the encodings, not just the one you're adding, that sometimes numbers that are negative when interpreted as signed are used.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19392/diffs?diff_id=1311340167&start_sha=3ed64c8a48fdc99aa72bc2b0033346fb908d6b28#cfc6b5284483868ee3ac2b54fc662eba573887b5_298_294)

Left only 0xC0A1E5CE, removed anything else including comments.

```
Isn't it simply the general custom of the VNC specification that actual encodings are positive, whereas psuedo-encodings/extensions are negative?
```

Initially, I assumed so. But I can't find any unambiguous declaration in the documentation, so I can't tell for sure.

This is derived from the packet data in the tvb at `offset` with length `4` and so it should still use that offset and length when adding it to the tree, even if there is a transformation (here, where a negative length indicates the compressed, possibly not plain text, format).

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19392/diffs?diff_id=1311340167&start_sha=3ed64c8a48fdc99aa72bc2b0033346fb908d6b28#cfc6b5284483868ee3ac2b54fc662eba573887b5_2253_2251)
Fixed
You added the offset, but it looks like the length is still 0. Can you make it 4?
Sure, added.
If you call `add_new_data_source` with the uncompressed tvb upon success, then the uncompressed bytes can be shown as an additional data source in the Packet Bytes pane.
Added, thanks!
It might be useful, both in the case where zlib is and is not present, to add an item to the tree with the compressed data, spanning its offset.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19392/diffs?diff_id=1311340167&start_sha=3ed64c8a48fdc99aa72bc2b0033346fb908d6b28#cfc6b5284483868ee3ac2b54fc662eba573887b5_2343_2343)
Added

https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#extended-clipboard-pseudo-encoding

> Microsoft HTML clipboard fragments.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dataxchg/html-clipboard-format

> CF_HTML is a text clipboard format, though always using UTF-8 encoding. Note that the use of UTF-8 here is an exception to the general rule that the Windows API uses UTF-16 for representing text strings, especially human-readable (i.e. localizable) strings.

So `ENC_UTF_8` is more appropriate than `ENC_ASCII`.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19392/diffs?diff_id=1311340167&start_sha=3ed64c8a48fdc99aa72bc2b0033346fb908d6b28#cfc6b5284483868ee3ac2b54fc662eba573887b5_2329_2329)
Thanks! Fixed.

Do you intend the RTF to be a `FT_STRING`? If so, then it shouldn't use `ENC_NA` above, but a text codec. (Even though right now `ENC_NA` and `ENC_ASCII` have the same value, this is not guaranteed and deprecated use.)

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19392/diffs?diff_id=1311340167&start_sha=3ed64c8a48fdc99aa72bc2b0033346fb908d6b28#cfc6b5284483868ee3ac2b54fc662eba573887b5_5290_5292)
A copy-paste mistake. Thanks, fixed.
Sorry, maybe I wasn't clear. If you use `ENC_NA` as the encoding when adding it, the field type here should probably be `FT_BYTES`. The field type can't be an encoding.
The fault is mine. Please take a look now.
